purpose: REFUSAL-parity vectors for the hand-maintained SIWC twin family (Plan 75-A section 7.3). Three copies: csd-sdk/packages/siwc/src/index.ts, cairn/src/lib/siwc.ts, cairn-wallet/src/core/siwc.ts. This file is DUPLICATED byte-for-byte into each repo (cross-repo checkouts do not exist in CI, the MF-27 lesson) and every copy's test pins sha256 of these bytes, so a drifted COPY reds. It pins test DATA across repos, never implementation bytes.

surfaces.build: buildSiwcMessage(fields). Present in all three twins. A refusal means buildSiwcMessage THROWS; an acceptance means it returns exactly `build.message` and siwcDigest returns exactly `build.digest`.
surfaces.verify: verifySiwc({message,sig64,pub33}, expected). Present in csd-siwc and cairn only; the wallet twin is a BUILDER (it signs, the relying party verifies), so a build-only twin skips every verify leg and pins the skipped ids.

vectors.label: lone surrogate in a signed field
vectors.why: utf8ToBytes maps an unpaired surrogate to U+FFFD, so two DIFFERENT messages collapse onto ONE digest and a signature over one verifies the other (siwcDigest is non-injective over arbitrary strings). The Python reference cannot encode one at all, which is the C1 cross-language class. Audit note: the wallet twin is KNOWN to lack this guard.

vectors.label: embedded newline in a signed field
vectors.why: A newline in a field value forges an extra message line, so a signed artifact can DISPLAY differently than it verifies. The build guard blocks every line terminator (\n \r U+2028 U+2029 U+0085 \v \f), and the parser's canonical round-trip refuses the forged message.

vectors.label: out-of-range time in Issued At
vectors.why: The RFC3339 shape regex passes 25:61:61 but Date.parse returns NaN, and every time bound is a > / >= comparison that is FALSE against NaN. Without the explicit NaN refusal one unparseable timestamp disables all of the clock bounds at once. Verify surface only: the builder deliberately does not range-check time values, so a build-only twin cannot carry this leg.

vectors.label: canonical minimal sign-in (no statement)
vectors.why: The paired happy path for R2 and R3: the exact call shape a relying party sends. Pins the canonical bytes AND the digest across all three twins, so a builder that drifts one byte reds here instead of shipping a signature no verifier accepts.
